verses: The red bows unbent were received, and are kept In store,—to reward service done for our land. Lo! here is a prince whose great merit we own; To him one I give from my heart with glad hand. The bells and the drums all in order are placed;— I'll feast the whole morning with this noble guest.

The red bows unbent were received, and are fixed On frames,—to await service done for our states. Lo! here is a prince who well merits the prize; With joy my whole heart in his presence dilates. The bells and the drums in good order all stand;— And this morning his place shall be on my right hand.

The red bows unbent were received, and are placed In cases,—to show how we merit revere. Lo! here is a prince such reward who deserves; For him in my heart's core the love is sincere. With our bells and our drums the court shall resound, While for him all the morning the pledge cup goes round.
